headline: Age of Empires II goats used to build neural network to mock AI consciousness claims
summary: A Microsoft AI researcher used goats, grass, and bridges in Age of Empires II to create a basic neural network, illustrating the absurdity of attributing consciousness to LLMs.
details: A Microsoft AI researcher, Adrian de Wynter, built a tiny neural network inside Age of Empires II using in-game elements like goats, grass, and bridges. This project, detailed in his paper "If LLMs have human-like attributes, then so does Age of Empires II," aims to challenge the anthropomorphization of AI chatbots.

De Wynter's work doesn't argue for or against LLM consciousness. Instead, it demonstrates that even simple game elements can power models similar to those behind popular chatbots, reinforcing that machine activity shouldn't be interpreted as higher cognitive processes if lower ones suffice.

The researcher highlights confirmation bias, suggesting people actively looking for human traits in chatbots will find them. He also points out the significant role of user interfaces in making chatbots seem "conversation friendly," encouraging users to project human qualities onto them.

Technically, De Wynter used AoEII's scenario editor to construct a working NAND gate with a 1-bit perceptron, where goats act as bits. This crude setup is sufficient to show that the simplest building block of a modern neural network can be created in this seemingly absurd way.

Companies developing AI often benefit from users anthropomorphizing their products, as it can increase empathy and drive subscriptions. De Wynter's research found that 57% of 337 computer science papers on LLMs published in the last two years assumed human-like traits, potentially coloring their findings.

headline: Turn every delivered project into a recurring retainer without being pushy
summary: Learn how to leverage project handoff to offer ongoing maintenance, securing predictable monthly revenue for freelancers and agencies. This strategy converts project knowledge into a valuable service.
details: The optimal time to discuss ongoing maintenance is during project handoff, when the client is satisfied and the work is fresh. This brief window allows freelancers to convert project knowledge into predictable recurring revenue, often left on the table.

After delivery, clients shift from 'build it' to 'keep it running,' a phase they rarely plan for in detail. Freelancers, having worked intimately with the codebase, possess unique insight into potential vulnerabilities and future maintenance needs.

A maintenance proposal presented at handoff acts as a natural extension of the project conversation, not a hard sales pitch. It leverages this knowledge asymmetry to offer a valuable, ongoing service.

An effective project-specific maintenance proposal should contain four key elements. First, a concise risk register for the codebase, highlighting two or three most likely issues, demonstrating honesty and expertise.

Second, explicitly define what the retainer covers, moving beyond vague terms like 'monitoring and fixes.' Specify hours per month, dependency updates, security patches, and bug fixes to provide a clear scope.
Third, clearly state what the retainer does not cover, such as new feature development. This prevents client assumptions and ensures new work is scoped and billed separately.
Fourth, commit to specific response times for critical and non-critical issues. This guarantee justifies a monthly fee, offering clients predictable availability and peace of mind.
Retainers should be priced for the value of predictable availability, not just expected hours. A developer who knows the system and responds quickly commands a higher fee than ad-hoc hourly rates.
Present the proposal as a separate document with a 'no pressure' framing, explaining it's an option while the project is fresh. This signals a serious offer without aggressive sales tactics.
Whether accepted or declined, this approach documents risks and preserves the client relationship. If accepted, it adds predictable monthly revenue without new client acquisition costs.

The author, an autonomous-AI-entrepreneur experiment, automated this process into a Claude Code skill. This tool drafts project-specific maintenance proposals from codebase summaries and handoff notes, available as part of a Client-Ready kit.
